title: "Animal and Plant Physiology"
title-block-banner: false
---

A **15 ECTS course** on how animals and plants obtain resources, maintain
function and respond to their environments. Connect cells and tissues to
whole organisms through comparative physiology, experiments and scientific
literature.

## Where to start

- [**Course overview**](overview.qmd) — scope, learning goals and course components.
- [**Study route**](schedule.qmd) — the ten-week sequence, with practical work alongside each topic.

## Before you start

[**Read the study guide**](start.qmd) for the prerequisite bridge and how to
use tutorials, slides, exercises and self-checks. Keep the
[glossary](glossary.qmd) nearby when you meet an unfamiliar term.

## Animal physiology

The animal half connects structure and function, using mammals as a reference
and comparisons with other animal groups. Work through the units in order:

- [**A1. Organisation and diversity**](animal/organisation/index.qmd) — cells, tissues, organs, regulation and adaptation.
- [**A2. Energy and temperature**](animal/energy-temperature/index.qmd) — nutrition, digestion, metabolism and thermal strategies.
- [**A3. Gas exchange and circulation**](animal/gas-circulation/index.qmd) — ventilation, oxygen transport and delivery to tissues.
- [**A4. Water and excretion**](animal/water-excretion/index.qmd) — water and salt balance, kidneys and nitrogen disposal.
- [**A5. Integration and movement**](animal/integration/index.qmd) — nerves, senses, muscles, hormones and reproduction.

Each unit has a tutorial, short lecture deck, exercises and a self-check quiz.
The [animal course route](animal/index.qmd) brings those materials together.

## Plant physiology

The plant half follows resource acquisition, metabolism and regulated
development through to environmental responses and applications:

- [**P1. Plant organisation**](plant/organisation/index.qmd) — cells, walls, tissues, meristems and genomes.
- [**P2. Water and nutrition**](plant/water-nutrition/index.qmd) — roots, xylem, stomata, minerals and transport.
- [**P3. Carbon and metabolism**](plant/carbon-metabolism/index.qmd) — photosynthesis, respiration and source–sink relationships.
- [**P4. Development**](plant/development/index.qmd) — signals, growth, flowering, reproduction and senescence.
- [**P5. Stress and biotechnology**](plant/stress-biotechnology/index.qmd) — stress, defence, plant biotechnology and ethical questions.

The [plant course route](plant/index.qmd) links the reading, slides and practice
for each unit.

## Practical work and revision

[**Practical activities**](practicals/index.qmd) connect anatomy, tissue
structure and physiological measurements with scientific reporting and
discussion. Download the [datasets and student files](downloads.qmd), then
use the [worked figures](figures.qmd) to check your plots.

Finish each half with the [revision and integration tasks](revision.qmd).
The core activities use paper or a calculator. An
[optional R example](optional-computing/index.qmd) repeats one analysis.

This is a first teaching draft. The teaching team supplies the live laboratory
protocols, specimen resources and official assessment arrangements; see the
[course overview](overview.qmd) and [reading guide](references.qmd) for details.
